# mdstudio

> mdstudio is an open-source, local-first Markdown editor and portability checker. It shows how your Markdown will render on GitHub, dev.to, Obsidian or a strict CommonMark engine, flags syntax that will not travel, and exports clean .md files. Formerly called Markdown Studio.

Write Markdown in a full-featured editor with a complete formatting toolbar and a live preview. The raw Markdown is the single source of truth: the preview shows what other platforms render, with no preview-only syntax. Drafts are saved in the browser (IndexedDB) with no account and are not uploaded unless the writer chooses to. An optional account can keep up to 5 chosen drafts in a cloud, and a verified account can publish one as a public, read-only page that expires within 7 days.

## What it does

- Target profiles: Strict CommonMark, GFM extended, GFM without HTML, Wiki notes. The preview, the checks and the toolbar warnings follow the chosen profile.
- Portability checker: flags raw HTML, local image paths, base64 images, wiki-links, math, Mermaid and trailing-space line breaks, with clickable issues that jump to the line.
- Rich Markdown: tables with cell navigation, task lists, footnotes, GitHub alerts, KaTeX math, Mermaid diagrams, syntax-highlighted code blocks.
- Import and export: open .md files, ZIP archives or whole folders, paste from Google Docs, Notion and the web; export clean UTF-8 Markdown (LF endings), standalone HTML, or every draft as a ZIP.
- Library: search drafts, filter by tag, organise them in folders, rename them, and go back to any earlier version with a side-by-side compare.
- Custom checker rules: turn rules on or off, add publication standards (title and description length, required front matter, heading structure) and your own text or regex rules, and share them as a JSON file.
- Works offline after the first visit and can be installed as an app.
- Optional AI writing helpers with the writer's own API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Keys stay in session memory and requests go directly from the browser to the provider.
- MIT licensed and open source. Self-host with Docker (`ghcr.io/deityhub/mdstudio` or `deityhub/mdstudio` on Docker Hub).

## Who it is for

- Technical bloggers publishing through GitHub and static site generators.
- Developers writing READMEs and documentation for GitHub.
- Obsidian users who share notes outside Obsidian.
- Documentation teams who need Markdown that renders the same in every tool.

## Common questions

- Is it open source? Yes, it is MIT licensed, and you can use it in the browser or self-host it.
- Are documents private? Yes by default. They stay in the browser; an account and the cloud are optional, and a draft is public only if the writer publishes it as a link that expires.
- How is it different from other Markdown editors? It checks portability across platforms instead of rendering Markdown its own way.

## Guides

- [Portable Markdown: why it renders differently everywhere](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-portability): the six things that break most often and a checklist
- [CommonMark vs GitHub Flavored Markdown](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/commonmark-vs-github-flavored-markdown): tables, task lists, strikethrough, footnotes, alerts
- [Obsidian to GitHub Markdown](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/obsidian-to-github-markdown): converting wiki-links, highlights, callouts and embeds
- [Writing Markdown for dev.to and Hashnode](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-for-devto-and-hashnode): front matter, images, raw HTML
- [Markdown line breaks and paragraphs](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-line-breaks): soft breaks, hard breaks and the portable choice
- [Markdown images](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-images): paths, hosted URLs, base64 and alt text
- [Math and Mermaid diagrams in Markdown](https://mdstudio.deityhub.com/guides/markdown-math-and-diagrams): where they render and what to do elsewhere
